<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. II.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 AND it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governour of Syria.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Octavius Cesar,</ns0:hi> (called <ns0:hi>Augustus,</ns0:hi> for his prosperous atchieve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments,) was the first <ns0:hi>Roman Emperor</ns0:hi> properly so called, (for <ns0:hi>Iulius Caesar</ns0:hi> had but the Title of <ns0:hi>Perpetual Dictator</ns0:hi>) In the forty second year of whose Reign Christ was Born. <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>in the one and thirtieth year</ns0:hi> Antiq. Cap. 10. <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> the great beeing at that time, <ns0:hi>King of Iudea</ns0:hi> (being so declared by the Senate of <ns0:hi>R<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>me</ns0:hi> near forty years before) it was the Cu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>om of the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> to take a p<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rticular account of the Numbers, and Qualities of all Persons, inhab<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ting Countries under their ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risdiction, in order to the laying of Taxes upon them. About the time of the Birth of Christ, there was a Decree issued from the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Emperor for such a <ns0:hi>Census,</ns0:hi> or account to be taken of the Jews, (who some think are here only understood by the Term, all the World) others think, that it was a Decree which reached all that part of the World, which was subject to the <ns0:hi>Ro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man</ns0:hi> Emperor. This trust it seemeth was committed to <ns0:hi>Cyreni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />us</ns0:hi> Governour of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> whether he was at that time Governour, or afterwards made Governour, and at this time only a Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />missioner, for this business is not agreed. That this <ns0:hi>Cyrenius</ns0:hi> was the same whom the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Historians call <ns0:hi>Quirinius,</ns0:hi> is pretty well agreed. Great indeavours are used to reconcile what <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith here, to <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Roman Historians,</ns0:hi> who make <ns0:hi>Varus</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>Quirinius,</ns0:hi> as this time the President of <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> (those who desire to be satisfyed as to those things may read Mr. <ns0:hi>Poel's Synopsis Criticorum,</ns0:hi> upon this Text, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>) where <ns0:hi>Civil Historians</ns0:hi> differ from what we have in holy Writ, we are ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liged to believe them mistaken, not the Penmen of holy Writ, who were giuded by an infallible Spirit. Leaving therefore those disputes, and in what Sense this <ns0:hi>Census,</ns0:hi> is called the first, or is said to be first begun, when <ns0:hi>Cyrenius</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Quirinius</ns0:hi> was president (as being of no great concern, for other Historians grant <ns0:hi>Qui<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rinius</ns0:hi> at this time a Commissioner with <ns0:hi>Cajus Caesar,</ns0:hi> and with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in Ten years after <ns0:hi>President,</ns0:hi> in Succession of <ns0:hi>Varus</ns0:hi>) let us ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther herein observe the wonderful Providence of God in the or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dering of things for the fulfilling of his Word, while we think of no such things, to which purpose doubtless this is premised by the Evangelist. According to the Counsel of God declared by his Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 5.2. Christ was to be Born at <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tropolis of Iudea,</ns0:hi> so the <ns0:hi>Chief Priests</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> tell <ns0:hi>Herod, Matth.</ns0:hi> 2.5. <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> his Mother, and <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> his supposed Father, lived at a great distance from <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi> a City of <ns0:hi>Galilee.</ns0:hi> God so ordereth it, that the <ns0:hi>Roman Emperor</ns0:hi> (under whose Power the Jews were at this time) orders a numbring of all his Subjects, either in all his Dominions at the same time, or at least in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> and an account to be taken of their Persons, and Qualities, in order to the laying Taxes upon them, to defray the charges of the <ns0:hi>Empire.</ns0:hi> The account o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the Jews being to be ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken according to their Tribes, those who belonged to each Tribe, were ordered to Convene in the Chief City belonging to the Tribe of which they were. <ns0:hi>I seph,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> were both of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah.</ns0:hi> This occasion brings them both to <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> being the Chief City of their Tr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>be to meet the <ns0:hi>Emperors</ns0:hi> Commission<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ers, So Christ came to be Born in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> according to the Word of the Lord, from which a Title shall not fail, and <ns0:hi>little Bethlehem</ns0:hi> becomes not the least amongst the thousands of <ns0:hi>Iu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dah,</ns0:hi> one coming out of it to be a <ns0:hi>Ruler in</ns0:hi> Israel, <ns0:hi>whose goings were of old even from everlasting.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:295" />4 And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, unto the city of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 7.42. 1 S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 16.4.</ns0:note> David, which is called Bethlehem because he was of the house and linage of David.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And so it was, that while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delive<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red.<ns0:note place="bottom">This was the occasion of <ns0:hi>Iosephs</ns0:hi> coming to <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> who either for fear of <ns0:hi>Herod,</ns0:hi> or for the convenience of his Trade, (tho he belonged to the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi>) was removed into <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> but he yieldeth obedience to the <ns0:hi>Civil Magistrates,</ns0:hi> and cometh to be <ns0:hi>enrolled,</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Court Books</ns0:hi> belonging to the <ns0:hi>Roman Em<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pire,</ns0:hi> to which by this Action he acknowledgeth himself a Subject, he also by this <ns0:hi>Act</ns0:hi> publickly declared both himself, and <ns0:hi>Mary his Wife</ns0:hi> to have been of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and of the Family of <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi> We are told it was the Custom of the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> to Enroll both Women and Children, however <ns0:hi>Marys</ns0:hi> Personal Attendance upon this Homage, might have been excused by her being great with Child, had not the Counsel of God so ordered it, that Christ should be Born there, this doubtless carried <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> along with <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seph,</ns0:hi> he having now (<ns0:hi>according</ns0:hi> to the Angels direction, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.20.24.) took her unto him as his Wife, while they were there, <ns0:hi>Maries</ns0:hi> time of <ns0:hi>Child-bearing was accomplished,</ns0:hi> we have the like Phrase, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 25.24.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 1.25.</ns0:note> she brought forth her first-born-son, and wrapped him in swadling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is <ns0:hi>Bucer</ns0:hi>'s Note, that in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> it is not <ns0:hi>her First-born-Son</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> her Son, the First-born, he was truly her Son, and <ns0:hi>her Son first-born,</ns0:hi> but he was not called <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> upon that account meerly, for he was <ns0:hi>the first-born of every Creature, Col.</ns0:hi> 1.15. he was the <ns0:hi>first-born</ns0:hi> also of <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry,</ns0:hi> but it cannot be from thence concluded, she had more Sons, (<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or where there is but <ns0:hi>one Son,</ns0:hi> he is the first-born.) <ns0:hi>And wra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ped him in Swadling Cloths, and laid him in a Manger,</ns0:hi> &c. whether the Inn was in the City, or in the Suburbs, adjoyning near to the City, is not material for us to know, nor considering the occasion of meeting at <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> at that day, and the num<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bers who upon that occasion must be there, is it at all strange, that Person of no higher Visible Quality then a <ns0:hi>Carpenter</ns0:hi> should not find a Room in the Inn, but be thrust into a Stable, nor was it un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />usual in those Countries for Men and Women to have Lodgings in the same Rooms where Beasts are kept, (it is no more then is at this Day in some places even in <ns0:hi>Europe.</ns0:hi>) Here the Virgin falls into her Labour, brings forth her Son, and Lodgeth him in a <ns0:hi>Man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger.</ns0:hi> God (by this) teaching all Christians to despise the High and Gay things of this World, he who, tho he was <ns0:hi>in the form of God, and thought it no Robbery to be equal with the Father,</ns0:hi> thus <ns0:hi>making himself of no Reputation—and being found in Fashon of a Man,</ns0:hi> thus <ns0:hi>humbling himself,</ns0:hi> as the Apostle speaks, <ns0:hi>Philip.</ns0:hi> 2.6, 7, 8.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And there were in the same country shepherds a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />biding in thefield, keeping <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the night watches.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> watch over their flocks by night.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> was a place about which were Pastures for Sheep, as appears from 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 17.15. There were Shepherds, abroad in the Night (for so the Word signifyeth) watching over their Flocks, whether the Phrase signifyeth (as some think) successive Watch<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />es such as are kept by Souldiers, and by the Priests, I cannot say. This maketh some think, that it is hardly probable, that our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour was Born in <ns0:hi>December</ns0:hi> in the midst of the Winter, that be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing no time when Shepherds use in the Night to be keeping their Flocks in the Field.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them, and they were sore afraid:<ns0:note place="bottom">Christ was promised to Men, who <ns0:hi>by their Occupation were Shepherds, Gen.</ns0:hi> 47.3. He himself was the <ns0:hi>Chief Shepherd,</ns0:hi> and the true Shepherd, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 10.1. The first Publication of his Birth, is made to <ns0:hi>Shepherds.</ns0:hi> Not to <ns0:hi>Shepherds</ns0:hi> that were idle, but busied in their honest Vocations keeping their Flocks. This Publication of his Birth is made by an Angel, whether the <ns0:hi>Angel Gabriel</ns0:hi> before mentioned, or another, is not certain. This <ns0:hi>An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gel,</ns0:hi> surprizeth the <ns0:hi>Shepherds, cometh upon them,</ns0:hi> thinking no such thing, but only minding their business. The <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> comes in a <ns0:hi>glorious appearance,</ns0:hi> probably an extraordinary Light, for it is said, it shone round about them, such an appearance of extra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ordinary Light is, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 9.30, 31. <ns0:hi>That they were sore afraid</ns0:hi> was but natural, we are naturally affected at suddain and unusual ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pearances with fear, and amazement.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And the angel said unto them, Fear not, for behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 For unto you is born this day in the city of Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid, a Saviour<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which is Christ the Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And this <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> a sign unto you, Ye shall find a babe wrapped in swadling cloths, lying in a man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger.<ns0:note place="bottom">Tho God in his appearances to his People, was wont so to appear, as to shew them cause to Revere his Majesty, yet he al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ways supported them that their Spirits might not fail, under those apprehensions and Consternations, The <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> bids them not to <ns0:hi>fear,</ns0:hi> for they had no reason to be afraid, he came not to bring them any affrighting Tidings, but <ns0:hi>Tidings of Ioy,</ns0:hi> and that not to them alone, but to all People, both Jews and Gentiles (for, to that Latitude the Text may be expounded) what was that? <ns0:hi>Vnto you is Born this Day in the City of</ns0:hi> David, <ns0:hi>a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.</ns0:hi> You have heard of the promises of the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> of a Christ that should come, and of the House of <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi> The promises of that Nature are this Day fulfilled, he is Born this very Day, <ns0:hi>unto you,</ns0:hi> but not to you alone, he had before told them, that his Ti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dings of Joy should extend to all Nations. <ns0:hi>And this shall be a Sign unto them,</ns0:hi> by this you shall know the truth of what I say, and you shall know also where to find him. <ns0:hi>In the City of</ns0:hi> David, (that is <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> as was said before) you <ns0:hi>shall find the Babe, wrapped in Swadling Cloaths, and laid in a Manger.</ns0:hi> Where you find such a <ns0:hi>Babe,</ns0:hi> that is he, therefore be not offended, at his low and mean Condition, let that be no Stumbling Block to you, I give it you as a Sign, by which you shall know him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And suddainly there was with the angel a mul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />titude of the heavenly host, praising God, and say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> good will towards men.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Nativity of our Saviour was published first by one <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> but it must be Celebrated by a Multitude of <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> who ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pear praising God upon this occasion. These are called the Lords host, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 103.20.21. not only because he useth them as his Arms, to destroy his Enemies, but also because of the order which is amongst them. How they Praised God is expressed, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. they Sang, <ns0:hi>Glory to God in the Highest. On Earth Peace and Good-will towards Men.</ns0:hi> The Words may be taken either <ns0:hi>Iudicatively,</ns0:hi> as signify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, That was come to pass that Day, by which God would have Glory, Men would have Peace, and the Good-will of God to the Sons of Men, w<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s unspeakably declared: Or <ns0:hi>Precatorily</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gels</ns0:hi> desiring Go<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> might have Glory, and that <ns0:hi>Peace might be on Earth</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and the <ns0:hi>Good-will of God</ns0:hi> published to the Sons of Men. But the <ns0:hi>Vulg<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>r Latin</ns0:hi> is most corrupt that rendereth these words, <ns0:hi>Peace to M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n of Good-will</ns0:hi>; when we consider that the <ns0:hi>Heaven<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Host</ns0:hi> was here <ns0:hi>praising God,</ns0:hi> it will appear very reasonable, to interpret these Words <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>dicatively.</ns0:hi> The Angelshereby decla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring their apprehensions, and the truth concerning this <ns0:hi>Act of Providence,</ns0:hi> no Act more declaring the Glory of Gods Power, Wisdom, or Goodness: nor more declaring his good will towards Men, and more conducing to Peace upon the Earth, whether by it we understand the Union of the Jews, and Gentiles, or that Peace of particular Souls, which <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>oweth from a justification by Faith in Christ, for tho the Text seemeth to speak of three things, <ns0:hi>Glory to God, Peace on Earth, and Good-will toward Men,</ns0:hi> yet indeed they are but two; the two latter differing only as the <ns0:hi>Cause,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Effect</ns0:hi>? The <ns0:hi>Good will of God</ns0:hi> is the cause, <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi> with, or amongst Men is the Effect, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.1. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.14, 15, 17.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:296" />15 And it came to pass, as the angels were gone away from them into heaven, the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the men the shepherds.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> shepherds said one to another, Let us now go even unto Bethlehem, and see this thing which is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known unto us.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And they came with hast, and found Mary and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And when they had seen <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they made known abroad the saying which was told them concerning this child.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And all they that heard <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> wondred at those things which were told them by the shepherds.<ns0:note place="bottom">It was Night, yet they delayed not to go, and make a search, according to the <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> and not in vain, they found <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Babe.</ns0:hi> Divine Revelations ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver deceive the Soul, that gives credit to them. Heaven and Earth may pass away, but nothing which God hath spoken shall pass away without its accomplishment. <ns0:hi>When they had seen it, they made known the saying,</ns0:hi> &c. They had no charge of Secrecy up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on them, so did well in publishing what was of such Universal concern for Men to know, Spiritual Morsels ought not to be Ate alone. The effect of their <ns0:hi>Relation,</ns0:hi> in the generality of the People that heard it, was the same which we have often met with, upon the Peoples seeing of Christs Miracles, <ns0:hi>viz. Amaze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Astonishment,</ns0:hi> we read nothing of their Faith. The first was a Natural Effect of a strange <ns0:hi>Relation.</ns0:hi> The other must have been the special Operation of God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 But Mary kept all these things, and pondered <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> in her heart.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told unto them.<ns0:note place="bottom">The different effect of these things upon the Generality of the People, upon <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> and upon the <ns0:hi>Shepherds</ns0:hi> is worthy of our notice. The People only wondered, thinking the Story of the Shepherds a strange Story, <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> suffereth them not to pass out of her thoughts, nor entertaineth them with a meer passion, which suddainly is extinguished, but she <ns0:hi>pondereth them in her Heart,</ns0:hi> both those things she had learned from her Husband, and what her self had heard from the Angel, and this also, which was rela<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted to her of or by the <ns0:hi>Shepherds.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Shepherds return,</ns0:hi> that is, to the care of their Flocks, Religion gives none a discharge from their secular Duties, the Disciples had a special Call, and Command, that left their Nets, and their Parents, and followed Christ. The <ns0:hi>Shepherds</ns0:hi> were only made occasional Preachers, <ns0:hi>pro h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>c vice</ns0:hi> they return, but <ns0:hi>Glorifying and Praising God for all the things they had heard, and seen, as it was told them,</ns0:hi> which argued, that they gave a firm and full Assent to them, and that they were the first Fruits of Believers under the Gospel-Dispensation. True Faith produceth great Joy, and Thanksgi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving to God, and needs must produce Joy, because of the Uni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on it maketh betwixt a Soul, and its desired object.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.31.</ns0:note> called JESUS, which was so named of the angel, before he was conceived in the womb.<ns0:note place="bottom">The time Prescribed by the Divine Law for Circumcision, was the Eighth Day, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.12. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 12.3. he was indeed the Law-giver, and as such not tyed to the observance of the Law. But he was also <ns0:hi>made of a Woman, made under the Law, Gal.</ns0:hi> 4.4. and the Law was, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 12.2. <ns0:hi>That if a Woman had conceived Seed, and Born a Man-Child in the Eighth Day, the Flesh of his fore-skin should be Circumcised.</ns0:hi> He was to make himself appear the Son of <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> and so this was Gods <ns0:hi>Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.10. with <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Seed after him, every Man-Child among you shall be Circumcised.</ns0:hi> This Law Christ was bound to <ns0:hi>fulfil,</ns0:hi> and by the fulfilling of it in this point, he shewed himself a <ns0:hi>Debtor to the whole</ns0:hi> Law, <ns0:hi>Galath.</ns0:hi> 5.3. and by his observance of it, he was to teach us our Duty. He was to be a <ns0:hi>Minister of the Circumcision, Rom.</ns0:hi> 15.8. and to the <ns0:hi>Circumcision</ns0:hi> which they would never have allowed him to be, had not he himself been Circumcised, upon which account <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> took <ns0:hi>Timothy,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Circumcised him, Acts</ns0:hi> 16.3. <ns0:hi>By his Circumcision also we were to be Circumcised, with the Cir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumcision made without Hands, in putting off the Body of the Sin of the Flesh, Coloss.</ns0:hi> 2.11. It was therefore reasonable and necessary that Christ should be Circumcised <ns0:hi>the eighth Day. His Name was called Iesus,</ns0:hi> it was in Circumcision before Wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness Publickly declared to be so, for God by his Angel had gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven him his Name, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.21. we read of four under the Old Testament, to whom God gave Names, before they were Born, <ns0:hi>Isaac, Gen.</ns0:hi> 17.19. <ns0:hi>Iosiah,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 13.2. <ns0:hi>Ishmael, Gen.</ns0:hi> 16.11. <ns0:hi>Cyrus, Isaiah</ns0:hi> 44.28. and in the New <ns0:hi>Testament</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> and to <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> Christ. Which lets us know the certain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty to God of future Contingencies, for tho the Parents of <ns0:hi>Ishmael,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Isaac, Iohn Baptist,</ns0:hi> and Christ, imposed those Names in obedience to the Command of God, and there was but a small time betwixt, the giving of these four their Names, and their Birth, yet the Case was otherwise as to <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cyrus.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="22">22 And when the days of her purification, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the law of Moses, were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> to the Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 As it is written in the law of the Lord, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 22.29.34.19.</ns0:note> Eve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 12.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> A pair of turtle-doves, or two young pigeons.<ns0:note place="bottom">In these Verses is a <ns0:hi>Record</ns0:hi> of the Virgins obedience to two Laws, The one concerning the <ns0:hi>Purification of the Woman after Child-Birth</ns0:hi>; the other concerning the presenting of the <ns0:hi>Male-Child</ns0:hi> before the Lord. We have the Law concerning <ns0:hi>Purifica<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, Levit.</ns0:hi> 12.4. throughout. The Sum was, That if a Wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man had brought forth a Male-Child, she should be unclean se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven Days, and after that continue in the Blood of her Puri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fying thirty three Days. If she brought forth a <ns0:hi>Female,</ns0:hi> she was to be unclean fourteen days, and afterward to continue in the Blood of her Purifying, Sixty Six days. So that the time of the Womans <ns0:hi>Purification</ns0:hi> after the Birth of a Female, was <ns0:hi>fourscore Days,</ns0:hi> for a <ns0:hi>Male</ns0:hi> (which was the present case) forty. After the Expiration of which time, she was to bring a Lamb of a Year old, for a Burnt-offering, and a <ns0:hi>young Pigeon or a Tur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tle-Dove,</ns0:hi> for a <ns0:hi>Sin-Offering,</ns0:hi> to the Priest to the Tabernacle, who was to offer it for her, and to make an Atonement. If she were Poor and not able to bring a Lamb (which seems the pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent case) then she was to bring only <ns0:hi>two Turtle-Doves,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>two young Pigeons,</ns0:hi> the one for a <ns0:hi>Burnt-Offering, the other for a Sin-Offering.</ns0:hi> The Evangelist takes no notice of any <ns0:hi>Lamb,</ns0:hi> but only <ns0:hi>a pair of Turtle-Doves,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>Two Young Pigeons.</ns0:hi> Which lets us know, she was Poor, and so obliged by the Law no further. <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> after her Forty Days were expired, cometh up to the Temple, to yield obedience to this Law. And not so only, but also to <ns0:hi>present her Child before the Lord.</ns0:hi> This depended upon two Laws. We find the one, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 13.2. where in remembrance of Gods sparing the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> when he smote the <ns0:hi>first Born of the Egyptians,</ns0:hi> he gave the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> this Law. <ns0:hi>Sanctify unto me all the first-Born, whatsoever openeth the Womb amongst the Children of</ns0:hi> Israel, <ns0:hi>both of Man and Beast it is mine.</ns0:hi> So <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 22.29. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 34.19. Instead of these, God took the <ns0:hi>Levites,</ns0:hi> as appears by <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 8.16. yet were the first-Born to be presented before the Lord, and <ns0:hi>Redeemed</ns0:hi> by the payment of Five Shekels apiece, for all those who were above the number of the <ns0:hi>Levites,</ns0:hi> as appeareth by <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 3.44, 45, 46, 47. and five <ns0:hi>Shekels</ns0:hi> was the Redemption-price of any Male upon a <ns0:hi>Singular</ns0:hi> Vow, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 27.6. For these two ends, after six Weeks, <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> come up to <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem.</ns0:hi>

That which <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Brentius,</ns0:hi> and o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther reformed Divines do think is much more probable, that he was some ordinary, plain Man of an obscure Quality, as to his Circumstances in the World.                      </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Song consists of an <ns0:hi>Elogium of Christ,</ns0:hi> whom <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> here calls the <ns0:hi>Lords Salvation.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>A light to lighten the Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>The Glory of</ns0:hi> Israel, and a Petition, that now the <ns0:hi>Lord would let him depart in Peace,</ns0:hi> but I shall take the Wordss in order. <ns0:hi>Lord lettest thou now thy Servant depart in Peace accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to thy Word.</ns0:hi> He desireth to dye, having now lived to see, what alone he desired Life for. It is a Speech much like <ns0:hi>Iacob, Gen.</ns0:hi> 46.30. when he had seen <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> (whom he thought lost) but spoken here upon a much more weighty Consideration. The Word Translated <ns0:hi>depart,</ns0:hi> signifies to absolve, and forgive, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6.37. to <ns0:hi>dismiss,</ns0:hi> and to <ns0:hi>deliver</ns0:hi> as from Bondage and Misery, it is used to express, the Death of good Men, by the <ns0:hi>Septuagint. Gen.</ns0:hi> 15.15. <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 20.29. and the Noun from it is used so by the Apostle, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.15. <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> owns God to be the Lord of his Life, who had the Power of it, and could alone dismiss him, and signifyeth himself to be an old Man, satisfyed with Days, willing to be at rest from the Miseries of this Life, but he beg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />geth to be dismissed, and to <ns0:hi>dye in Peace,</ns0:hi> that is, <ns0:hi>happily,</ns0:hi> see <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 15.15. 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 22.20. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 4.8. <ns0:hi>According to thy Word,</ns0:hi> that is, thy promise mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 26. But the putting of these Words in before those Words <ns0:hi>in Peace,</ns0:hi> seems to im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />port that he could not dye in peace before he had seen Gods Word fulfilled to him, in which he had made him to hope. <ns0:hi>For mine Eyes have seen thy Salvation,</ns0:hi> that is, thy Christ according to the Revelation I had from thee. <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> had a special Revelation of a Corporeal sight of Christ, he could not dye happily, till he had had that. None of us can <ns0:hi>dye in Peace,</ns0:hi> till we have seen the Lords Salvation with a spiritual Eye, and made Application of the promises of the Gospel, in the more general Revelation of his Word, <ns0:hi>thy Salvation, which thou hast prepared before the Face of all People.</ns0:hi> That is, the <ns0:hi>Author</ns0:hi> of Salvation, for <ns0:hi>there is no Salvation in any other, Acts</ns0:hi> 4.12. <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> declares that this Salvation was prepared for all People, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 11.10. he was prophesied of as <ns0:hi>an Ensign for the People, to it shall the Gentiles seek</ns0:hi> so <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 52.10. <ns0:hi>The Lord hath made bare his holy Arm in the Eyes of all the Nations, and all the ends of the Earth shall see the Salvation of our God.</ns0:hi> So <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 98.2. <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> speaks the same thing more particularly, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 32. <ns0:hi>A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the Glory of thy People</ns0:hi> Israel. All the People mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 32. were either <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iews. Simeon</ns0:hi> here prophesieth, that Christ should <ns0:hi>lighten</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> The State of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> (by whom were understood all the People in the World (except the Jews) is often in Scripture, expressed under the Notion of <ns0:hi>darkness,</ns0:hi> both in respect of the Ignorance of the true God, which was amongst them, and of their <ns0:hi>Idolatry</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Superstition,</ns0:hi> and their leud and wicked Lives much proportioned to their Religion. Hence <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> is said to be sent to the Gentiles, to <ns0:hi>turn them from Darkness to Light, Acts</ns0:hi> 26.18. Christ is called <ns0:hi>Light, Iohn</ns0:hi> 8.12. <ns0:hi>I am the Light of the World, he that followeth me shall not Walk in Dark<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, but shall have the Light of Life.</ns0:hi> So <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 9.5. Confor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mable to the old Prophecies, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 60.1. <ns0:hi>Arise, Shine, for the Light is come.—v.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Behold the Darkness shall cover the Earth, and Gross darkness the People, but the Lord shall a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rise upon thee.—v.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>And the Gentiles shall come to thy Light.</ns0:hi> And speaking of Christ. <ns0:hi>I will also give thee for a Light to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

               <ns0:p n="33">33 And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Brentius</ns0:hi> Notes on this Text. <ns0:hi>Non admirantur quia non Credunt, sed quia credunt, ideo admirantur.</ns0:hi> They did not admire because they did not believe, but because they believed, therefore they marvelled. They had <ns0:hi>Revelations</ns0:hi> what Christ was, the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> had appeared to <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Zachary,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elizabeth,</ns0:hi> the Wise-men had come from the East (if as some think they came so soon) yet they <ns0:hi>marvelled,</ns0:hi> they did not Contemn and mock at these things, but certainly neither did they fully understand them, but in the General <ns0:hi>believed</ns0:hi> the Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Revelation. I do doubt whether before Christ was <ns0:hi>declared to be the Son of God with Power,</ns0:hi> by his Resurrection from the Dead, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.3, 4. either <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> or Christs own Disciples did stea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dily and firmly believe, that <ns0:hi>Christ was the Eternal Son of God,</ns0:hi> tho it is clear that before that time, they believed him to be sent of God, and a <ns0:hi>great Prophet,</ns0:hi> nay the <ns0:hi>promised Messias,</ns0:hi> the Christ of God, and generally believed what was spoken of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> and the Christ belonged to him, but whether they did rightly understand that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was to be <ns0:hi>God-man</ns0:hi> I can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not tell. <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist</ns0:hi> seemeth clearest in the Case, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so made a famous Confession of it, but many things we Read of <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> afterward which speak even <ns0:hi>Peters</ns0:hi> Faith in the case, rather the <ns0:hi>Embryo</ns0:hi> of Faith, than a fixed and perfect Faith. But I impose nothing here on my <ns0:hi>Reader,</ns0:hi> let him judge as he seeth reason, supposing a fixed firm Faith in this Case, yet they might Marvel, for Christ <ns0:hi>is to be admired of them that believe,</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And Simeon blessed them, and said unto Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry his mother, Behold, this <ns0:hi>child</ns0:hi> is set for the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Is. 8.14. Rom. 9.32, 33.</ns0:note> fall and rising again of many in Israel, and for a <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 28.22.</ns0:note> sign which shall be spoken against.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 (Yea, a <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 19.25.</ns0:note> sword shall pierce through thy own soul also) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> blessed them, some may question how it was that <ns0:hi>Si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />meon</ns0:hi> blessed Christ, when as the Apostle tells us, The <ns0:hi>lesser is blessed of the greater.</ns0:hi> But we must distinguish, betwixt a <ns0:hi>Prophetical Blessing,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Iocob</ns0:hi> blessed his Sons, which was nothing but a Prediction how God would bless them. 2. An <ns0:hi>Authorita<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tive Blessing,</ns0:hi> as the Priests blessed the People in the Name of the Lord, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 6. Which is nothing but a pronouncing them blessed by Authority from God, whom God hath blessed. 3. a <ns0:hi>Charitable or Precatory Blessing.</ns0:hi> Praying God to Bless them. Thus Inferiors may bless Superiors, as well as Superiors may bless Inferiors. The first or last or both those is to be under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood here, not the second. <ns0:hi>And he said to</ns0:hi> Mary <ns0:hi>his Mother.</ns0:hi> Not to <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> who he knew was not his Natural, but Legal and Reputed Father. <ns0:hi>Behold this Child is set for the fall,</ns0:hi> &c. that by the <ns0:hi>fall</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>rising again,</ns0:hi> is here meant the Salvation and Damnation of many is doubted by no valuable Interpreters. The Apostle so applyeth, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 8.14. where he is said to be <ns0:hi>for a Stone of stumbling, and for a Rock of offence, to both the Houses of</ns0:hi> Israel, <ns0:hi>for a Gin, and for a Snare, to the In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />habitants of</ns0:hi> Jerusalem, <ns0:hi>and many amongst them shall Stum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken,</ns0:hi> so doth <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.8. neither is it more then Christ telleth us, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 9.39. <ns0:hi>For Iudgment I am come into this World, that they which see not might see, and that they which see might be made blind.</ns0:hi> Accordingly the Apostle saith, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.16. that they were <ns0:hi>to some, the Savour of Death unto Death, to others the Savour of Life unto Life.</ns0:hi> The rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son is, because they that <ns0:hi>believe in him shall be saved,</ns0:hi> they that believe <ns0:hi>not shall be Damned, Mar.</ns0:hi> 16.16. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.19.36. This is now granted on all Hands, That Christ will be the occasion of many Peoples Damnation, even all that reject, and oppose them, and believe not in him, and the cause of many Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples Salvation, even all that shall be saved. <ns0:hi>For there is no o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther name given under Heaven, by which any can be saved, Acts</ns0:hi> 4.12. see <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.44. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.4.5. and it is ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />servable, that the Salvation of Souls by Christ is expressed by the Term <ns0:hi>Rising.</ns0:hi> So as all are fallen, <ns0:hi>Eph,</ns0:hi> 2.1. and have need of the application of a greater Power to them for their Salvation, then an <ns0:hi>under-propping</ns0:hi> of the innate power of their Wills. But the great question is about <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>is set,</ns0:hi> whether it signify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth only, an event or some Counsel and Ordination of God, let us compare it with other Texts, where the same Word is used, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 1.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                     </ns0:gap> without the fore knowledge of God, or how Go<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap> should have any such fore-knowledge, without a previous Act of his Will, determining the thing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> let any one consider, in the mean time it is freely granted, that the intervening of Mens Unbelief, and M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">

                     </ns0:gap>ce, and Opposition to Christ, and his Gospel is the Proximate Meritorious Cause of the fall of any Soul by occasion of him. It follows. <ns0:hi>And for a Sign that shall be spoken against.</ns0:hi> Such a Mark as <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> speaks of, <ns0:hi>Iob.</ns0:hi> 16.12. or such a <ns0:hi>Sign</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> speaketh of, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 8.18. <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> here prophesieth. That Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t and his Ministers and People, should be Rediculed, and all the Arrowes of ungodly Men, should be shot again<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t him, which proved true in that Age as to Christ, and his Apostles and in succeeding Ages as to all that derive from him, and will so hold to the end of the World; <ns0:hi>Yea, a Sword shall pierce through thine own Soul also,</ns0:hi> as the Irons entred into the Soul of <ns0:hi>Ioseph, Psal.</ns0:hi> 10<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>.18. He tells the <ns0:hi>Virgin</ns0:hi> her Soul should be wounded with the Reproaches and Indignities, which should be offered to this blessed Babe, as it proved after<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards, when she heard him Reviled, and saw him Crucifyed. <ns0:hi>That the thoughts of many Hearts may be revealed.</ns0:hi> The Gospel-times, especially <ns0:hi>times of Persecution</ns0:hi> will discover, whom God hath chosen, and whom he hath not, by discovering the thoughts of their Hearts, it will then be seen who will re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive, and who will reject the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> who is on his side, and who will be against him. The Term [<ns0:hi>That</ns0:hi>] doth denote the <ns0:hi>Consequent</ns0:hi> not the <ns0:hi>Effect.</ns0:hi> The Preaching of the Gospel is the Lords <ns0:hi>Fan,</ns0:hi> by which he purgeth his Floor. Persecution is the Lords Sieve, by which he winnoweth Churches, and separateth the Dirt, and Darnel, and Tares from the Wheat. Gospel-times, and times of Persecution are both of them times which make great Discovery of Mens Spirits.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:297" />36 And there was one Anna a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser, she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And she <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi> with fasting and prayers night and day.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 And she coming in that instant, gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 15.43. Ver. 25.44.</ns0:note> looked for redemption in <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Jerusalem.<ns0:note place="bottom">God took a care that our Saviours Nativity should be fully attested. To the Testimony of the <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Wise-men,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Shepherds, Simeon</ns0:hi> here is added another. It is that of <ns0:hi>Anna</ns0:hi> who is described here by her <ns0:hi>Tribe,</ns0:hi> and by her <ns0:hi>Father.</ns0:hi> She was of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Aser,</ns0:hi> one of the meanest Tribes, and of those Ten Tribes that were carried into the Captivity of <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> having before made a Defection (under the Conduct of <ns0:hi>Ierobo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />am,</ns0:hi> both from the House of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and from the true Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship of God. But tho the Generality did so, yet many parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular Persons removed, to injoy the true Worship of God, and joyned themselves to <ns0:hi>Iudah, Ier.</ns0:hi> 50.4. it was prophecyed, <ns0:hi>that the Children of</ns0:hi> Israel <ns0:hi>should come, they, and the Children of</ns0:hi> Judah <ns0:hi>together going, and Weeping to seek the Lord their God.</ns0:hi> What her Father <ns0:hi>Phanuel</ns0:hi> was, we read not, she is also further said to be a <ns0:hi>Prophetess.</ns0:hi> Such there were amongst the Jews, we read of <ns0:hi>Deborah, Miriam,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Huldah,</ns0:hi> to whom King <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>siah</ns0:hi> sent. They were called <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Prophetesses</ns0:hi> who revealed the Will of God unto the People, but in the <ns0:hi>Old Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stament</ns0:hi> it most generall signifyed, such as God inabled to fore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tell things which were to come. The Spirit of <ns0:hi>Prophecy</ns0:hi> had much failed amongst the Jews <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or four hundred years before Christ, about Christs coming it began to <ns0:hi>revive.</ns0:hi> This Wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man seems to have been upward of a hundred years old, if we account the eighty four years here mentioned from her Widow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood, not so, if we count them from her Birth. She was but seven years Married, all the rest of her life she had spent in Widow-hood. <ns0:hi>S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e departed not from the Temple Night or Day.</ns0:hi> That is, she was frequently there, giving up her self wholly to Religious Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ercises. <ns0:hi>Prayer</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Fasting,</ns0:hi> that she might be more fit for <ns0:hi>Pray<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er.</ns0:hi> This Woman coming in at that instant, where <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> took up Christ in his Arms, <ns0:hi>&c. gave thanks likewise unto the Lord,</ns0:hi> and spake of him to such as she knew in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> who look<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed for the Redemption of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> There is no place where God hath had a Name, but how ever it be Corrupted, and Debauched, hath a number, that keep close to God. God in <ns0:hi>Ahabs</ns0:hi> time had seven thousand in <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> And in this most Corrupt time, there was a <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and an <ns0:hi>Anna,</ns0:hi> and also others who had a true No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion and Expectation of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and these the holy Ghost taketh more notice of then of all the <ns0:hi>Iewish Doctors,</ns0:hi> all the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharis<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>es,</ns0:hi> whose Names are rolled, while what these Persons said, and did shall remain for a Memorial of them, wherever the Gospel shall be Preached to the end of the World.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And when they had performed all things ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.<ns0:note place="bottom">If the Wise-men mentioned, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 2.1. had been with <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> before this time, it is more then probable that <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> would have made an end of Christ, at this time, therefore certainly it was after this time. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith nothing of what we have, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 13, 14, 15.19, 20, 21, 22, 23. of <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> going into <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> upon the Admonition of the <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> nor his coming back, but both <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> agree in their dwelling at <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> which he calleth <ns0:hi>their own City,</ns0:hi> for there <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> dwelt, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. How after this the Wise-men came to find him at <ns0:hi>Bethlehem, Matth.</ns0:hi> 2. the Scripture hath not told us. It is very Idle for any to say <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> dwelt there, for then he would not have taken up his <ns0:hi>Inn</ns0:hi> there, nor been put to such a stress, as to have his Wife bring forth in a Stable, besides it is apparent from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. and this Verse, and from <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 2.23. that he dwelt at <ns0:hi>Naza<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />reth.</ns0:hi> God who ordered the motion of the Wise-men, and their instructions to be sent to <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> to look for Christ, could easily find <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> some business to be done there at that time, whether some business of his Trade, or some Visit to his Friends we cannot say.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Ver. 52.</ns0:note> And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Verse shortly summeth up all that we have in the Gospel, of the History of the first twelve years of our Saviours Life. Tho there could be no Accession to the perfection of the Divine Nature in Christ, yet as to his humane Nature, he was (as we are) capable of Accession of Habits, and Wisdom and Knowlege, for tho the Divine Nature was personally United to the humane Nature, yet there was no Communication of Properties.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 Now his parents went to <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 23.14<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 17. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 34.23.</ns0:note> Jerusalem every year <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 16.1.</ns0:note> at the feast of the passover.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Law of God enjoyned all the <ns0:hi>Males</ns0:hi> of the Israelites to appear at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> before him, three times each year, of which the Feast of Unleavened Bread was one, but the Women seem not to have been all under the same Obligation, but many of them went, of which <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> was one, but we read not of Christs going, till he was <ns0:hi>twelve years Old.</ns0:hi> Some think that the Wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men used to go once in a year, we read that <ns0:hi>Elkanahs</ns0:hi> Wife went, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 1.5, 6, 7. but whether they generally did so or no, the Scripture saith not. One thing is observable. The <ns0:hi>Phari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sees</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> had in those days much Corrupted the <ns0:hi>Worship of God</ns0:hi> by their <ns0:hi>Traditions,</ns0:hi> yet they retained the substance of Gods Institutions, we find both our Saviour and his Disciples, and other People of God, not wholly forsaking the Jewish Church, because of its Corruptions, yet we cannot think they joyned with them in any thing of their <ns0:hi>Will Worship,</ns0:hi> from whence we may learn a tenderness as to a Total Separation <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rom a Church, and the lawfulness of attending Divine Ministrations, tho attended with usages, which we approve not of, provided there be no Idolatry in the Service.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And when he was twelve year old, they went up to Jerusalem, after the custom of the feast.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is said by those who are learned in the Jewish Writings, that till a Child was of this Age<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> he was not obliged by the Law to go. We have in Scripture nothing to ascertain us in the Case, it is certain that our Saviour went at this Age, <ns0:hi>after the Custom of the Feast,</ns0:hi> that is, so as to be there about the fourteenth Day of the Month, <ns0:hi>Nisan.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 And when they had fulfilled the days, as they returned, the child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem, and Joseph and his mother knew not <ns0:hi>of it.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 But they supposing him to have been in the company, went a days journey, and they sought him among <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> kinsfolk and among their acquaintance,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 And when they found him not, they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him.<ns0:note place="bottom">The feast of the Passover, and of <ns0:hi>Unleavened Bread</ns0:hi> held seven Days, during which time <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> stayed in <ns0:hi>Ieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem,</ns0:hi> and then returned, they usually both went to and return<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed from these Feasts in great Troops, or Companies. Christ tarried behind, <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> thinking he had been in the Company, missed him not, they return to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> to seek him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 And it came to pass, that after three days, they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the Doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.<ns0:note place="bottom">After three Days possibly here is to be understood from the time they first went from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> one Day they went for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward in their Journey, a second Day they were coming back, the third Day they found him, for it cannot be thought they should be in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> three days before they found him, con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sidering that they found him in the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> which it is likely was the first place they sought for him in. It should seem that the <ns0:hi>Doctors</ns0:hi> of the Law gave a general liberty to any, to propound any Questions to them about the Law of God, to which they gave Answers. But it is very probable, that something more then ordinary appeared in him, that they admitted him to <ns0:hi>Sit</ns0:hi> a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst them, for tho themselves sate on Benches, yet their Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ditors usually sate at their Feet, hence we read of <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi>'s being brought up at the feet of <ns0:hi>Gamaliel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>

                  </ns0:note> all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.<ns0:note place="bottom">What was the subject matter of the <ns0:hi>Doctors</ns0:hi> and Christs Discour<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses, is Vainly questioned, only in the general we may be assured it was something about the Divine Law, what the particular Themes or Subjects were, is not material for us to inquire. Our Saviour so answered their questions, as they were all astonished.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:297" />48 And when they saw him, they were amazed, And his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>lt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.<ns0:note place="bottom">Tho something must be allowed to a Womans passions, and a Mothers indulgence, yet one would think, that especially con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sidering where they found him, and what doing, she should not have spoken thus unto him, had she had, a clear, and distinct knowledge of his Divine Nature, in Union with her Flesh; she speaks to him with the authority of a Mother, Why hast thou thus dealt with us?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Fathers bu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siness?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.45. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 18.34</ns0:note> they understood not the saying, which he spake unto them.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some read it—<ns0:hi>that I must be in my Fathers House,</ns0:hi> then the Sense must be, Why did you seek me in any other place then the <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> that is<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> my <ns0:hi>Fathers House,</ns0:hi> there lyeth my Bu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siness. But the Phrase seemeth rather to signify as we Translate it. He doth here signify that <ns0:hi>God was his Father,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> might have known not only from the <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Angel,</ns0:hi> but because she had not known Man, but she did not yet fully un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand his Divine Office as <ns0:hi>Mediator</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and the great <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised, that should reveal the Will of God, to People, much less did she yet fully and distinctly understand, that he was by <ns0:hi>Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture the Eternal Son of God.</ns0:hi> She believed so much as was revealed to her clearly, concerning Christ. <ns0:hi>It is said they understood not the saying, which he spake unto them,</ns0:hi> they had not a clear, and distinct understanding of<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> them. In the mean time from these Words of our Saviour, and this Fact of his. We may learn, <ns0:hi>That Inferiours are not in all things under the Power of their most Natural Superiors.</ns0:hi> Particularly not in such things wherein they cannot yield obedience to them, without a disobe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dience unto God. There are some Cases wherein instead of o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />beying, we are bound <ns0:hi>to hate both Father and Mother</ns0:hi> by our Saviours Precept.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them, But his mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther kept all these sayings in her heart.<ns0:note place="bottom">We left him at <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> after <ns0:hi>Maries Purification, v.</ns0:hi> 39. we find him at <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi> now at twelve years old. We shall now read no more of him till <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3.23. when he came to <ns0:hi>be about thirty years of Age.</ns0:hi> What he did in the mean time, is a business of too much Curiosity for us to inquire, and of very lit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tle Significancy to us if we knew. Some think he wrought with his Father upon his Trade; as I cannot tell how to prove it, so I know nothing against it. It is not like he was sent to any of the <ns0:hi>Schools</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> as he who could Argue with the Doctors pertinently at twelve years of Age, and to whom the Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit was given not by measure, had no need of their instructions: So their <ns0:hi>Academies</ns0:hi> were not such as we can reasonably think, that <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> should seek any Education for him in them, and I know no reason why we should think, that he who abhorred not the <ns0:hi>Womb of the Virgin,</ns0:hi> nor a <ns0:hi>Stable,</ns0:hi> nor a <ns0:hi>Manger</ns0:hi> should abhor the Works of an honest Vocation, and not much more abhor an idle Life. But we dispute about these things in vain, being such as to which we can never be satisfied (God having hid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den them from our knowledge) what is for our Instruction is told us, <ns0:hi>He was Subject unto his Parents.</ns0:hi> This teacheth the greatest and highest Mortals, to <ns0:hi>honour their Fathers and Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers. Which</ns0:hi> (saith the Apostle) is the first <ns0:hi>Commandement with promise. Solomon</ns0:hi> honour'd his Mother, and behold a grea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter then <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi> is here, paying his Homage also both to the Womb that bare him, and to his (supposed) Father that provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded for him, and protected him. <ns0:hi>But his Mother kept all these sayings in her Heart. Mary</ns0:hi> was no forgetful hearer, some things she did not yet clearly understand, but she kept them in her Heart, and those who do so as to Gods Word, shall in time un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 And Jesus <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 40.</ns0:note> increased in wisdom and <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>age.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> stature, and in favour with God and man.<ns0:note place="bottom">If any ask how he, who was the <ns0:hi>Eternal Wisdom of the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther</ns0:hi> (who is the only wi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e God) increased in Wisdom, they must know that all things in Scripture, which are spoken of Christ, are not spoken with respect to his entire Person, but with respect to the one, or the other Nature United in that Person, he increa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed in <ns0:hi>Wisdom,</ns0:hi> as he did in Age, or Stature, with respect to his Humane, not to his Divine Nature. And, as God daily Magnify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed his Grace and Favour toward him, so he gave him Favour with the Neighbourhood, and People of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> so as that when he came forth to be a Publick Minister, he came forth as a Bishop, (the chief Bishop of <ns0:hi>Souls</ns0:hi> especially) ought to do, <ns0:hi>Having a good Repute even of those who were without.</ns0:hi> And thus we leave our Saviours History<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> for about eighteen years of which the History of the Gospel tells us nothing.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
